activities.prompt: Partida de 8 rondas para repasar el tema jugando.

rounds.prompt: Which detail explains the project's limited reach?
rounds.context: The mentoring scheme received enthusiastic feedback, but it operated in only two neighbourhoods and relied on a small pool of mentors.

options.text: Participants gave no feedback.
It operated in every neighbourhood.
It had a restricted geographical and human capacity.

rounds.explanation: Two neighbourhoods and few mentors explain why the positive results cannot be generalised widely.

rounds.context: The shared office reduced rent, but workers reported more interruptions and fewer quiet periods for complex tasks.

options.text: Lower cost came with less concentration.
Rent increased because interruptions fell.
Complex tasks became unnecessary.

rounds.explanation: The two clauses present a financial gain and a working-condition cost.

rounds.prompt: What is the function of the example?
rounds.context: The policy reduced waste in several departments. For instance, the catering team began ordering smaller quantities more frequently.

options.text: It proves every department acted identically.
It contradicts the policy.
It illustrates how the policy worked.

rounds.explanation: For instance introduces a concrete example of reducing waste.

rounds.prompt: Why does the writer mention the failed pilot?
rounds.context: The first pilot failed because residents were not told how the new system worked. The revised version began with demonstrations, after which participation improved.

options.text: To explain why demonstrations were cancelled.
To prove the system can never work.
To show how communication affected participation.

rounds.explanation: The contrast between the two pilots connects explanation with improved participation.

rounds.prompt: What is the main point of the passage?
rounds.context: A small town replaced several car journeys with a shared electric shuttle. The service is not a complete solution, but it has connected older residents with shops and clinics.

options.text: The town has removed every private car.
The shuttle service is cheaper than every alternative.
A limited transport scheme has produced useful social benefits.

rounds.explanation: The passage balances a limitation with the practical connections the shuttle provides.

rounds.prompt: What is not known from the passage?
rounds.context: The library's new app increased reservations in its first month. The report does not compare users with people who never downloaded it.

options.text: That a new app was introduced.
Whether non-users would have made reservations.
That the report considered reservations.

rounds.explanation: The report explicitly omits comparison with non-users.

rounds.context: The museum's digital catalogue was launched in April. Curators added photographs gradually because many older records had to be checked first.

options.text: The catalogue launched in April.
The museum closed in April.
The photographs were taken by visitors.

rounds.explanation: The launch month is directly stated; the other options contradict or add unsupported information.

rounds.context: The library introduced self-service returns. Staff were not removed; instead, they spent more time helping visitors find specialist material.

options.text: Specialist material was removed.
Automation changed staff duties rather than eliminating staff.
The library stopped accepting returns.

rounds.explanation: The passage explicitly contrasts changed duties with staff removal.

activities.explanation: Al terminar la partida verás la media de aciertos y la explicación de cada ronda fallada.

activities.instructions: Colócate en el carril de la respuesta correcta antes de cruzar cada puerta.
activities.prompt: Partida de 8 rondas para repasar el tema jugando.

rounds.prompt: What is the most cautious summary?
rounds.context: The pilot attracted volunteers quickly but required more staff coordination than expected. The organisers will continue it while revising registration.

options.text: It attracted no interest.
It has failed and will end.
It has potential but needs a more efficient process.

rounds.explanation: The continuation decision shows potential, while the registration revision addresses the coordination problem.

rounds.prompt: Which inference follows from the final sentence?
rounds.context: The council published the raw survey responses alongside its summary. This allowed residents to check whether the conclusions reflected the original answers.

options.text: The survey had no conclusions.
The council wanted the process to be transparent.
The raw responses were destroyed.

rounds.explanation: Publishing raw responses enables checking and therefore supports an inference of transparency.

rounds.context: The archive digitised 15,000 pages during its first year. Staff then slowed the project to check names and dates more carefully.

options.text: 15,000 pages were digitised in year one.
All pages were checked before digitisation.
The project ended after year one.

rounds.explanation: The number and period are stated explicitly.

rounds.prompt: What can be inferred from the room's use?
rounds.context: Employees reserved the quiet room mainly before presentations and complex negotiations. They rarely used it for routine email.

options.text: Routine email required special equipment.
They used it for every task.
They valued it for demanding preparation.

rounds.explanation: The pattern of reservations links the room with demanding preparation.

rounds.prompt: Which statement best qualifies the result?
rounds.context: A new timetable reduced delays on two routes during its first month. The team will monitor other routes before recommending the change more widely.

options.text: The result is encouraging but limited.
No further monitoring is needed.
The timetable failed on both routes.

rounds.explanation: Two routes and one month provide an encouraging but limited result.

rounds.context: The course attracted more applicants after its evening option was introduced. Attendance was steady, although the organisers did not measure completion rates.

options.text: The organisers lacked one measure.
The evening option attracted interest.
The course had a higher completion rate.

rounds.explanation: The passage mentions applicants and attendance but gives no completion-rate comparison.

rounds.prompt: What can be inferred about the policy?
rounds.context: The policy increased recycling in offices with clear collection points. In buildings where bins were hidden, the effect was negligible.

options.text: Hidden bins increased recycling.
Offices had no collection points.
Implementation conditions influenced its success.

rounds.explanation: The contrast between visible and hidden collection points shows that implementation mattered.

rounds.context: The first design was cheaper to build, while the second used more durable materials. The committee selected the second after considering maintenance over ten years.

options.text: The first design was more durable.
Long-term maintenance outweighed the initial saving.
The committee ignored future costs.

rounds.explanation: The selection after a ten-year maintenance review implies that durability mattered more than the initial price.

activities.explanation: Al terminar la partida verás la media de aciertos y la explicación de cada ronda fallada.
